title: Popover API overview and support-aware use
learningObjectives: Explain popover api overview and support-aware use and choose an appropriate native HTML interaction.

understand.concept: The Popover API provides declarative and programmatic ways to show content in the top layer. HTML popover attributes include popover and popovertarget; JavaScript methods include showPopover(), hidePopover(), and togglePopover(). Popovers are non-modal by default and do not make the rest of the page inert.
understand.whyItMatters: A popover is not a replacement for every menu or dialog pattern. Choose semantics that match the interaction, check browser support, and ensure keyboard and assistive technology behaviour is appropriate.
understand.analogy: A popover is a small layer of additional content that can appear above the page without turning the rest of the page into a modal conversation.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual dialog, disclosure, and focus behaviour follows HTML and accessibility platform rules.

explain.narrative: The button toggles a non-modal popover using declarative HTML. The close button hides it.

examples.code: Use semantic HTML and clear labels.
examples.explanation: The button toggles a non-modal popover using declarative HTML. The close button hides it.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered native disclosure, dialog, or popover example.

practise.guidedTask: Build a help popover with a clear trigger and close action. Check keyboard behaviour and browser support, and explain why it is not a modal dialog.
practise.independentTask: Build an interaction using native HTML first. Test keyboard operation, accessible naming, focus behaviour, and browser support.
hints: Prefer native controls when they meet the requirement.
Give dialogs and popovers clear accessible names and labels.
Test focus entry, dismissal, and return.

questions.prompt: What should guide the choice between native and custom widgets?
options: Whether a native control meets the interaction requirement
Whether a custom widget looks more decorative
Whether ARIA can replace all HTML semantics
questions.answer: Whether a native control meets the interaction requirement
questions.explanation: Native controls are usually the safer choice unless the interaction genuinely requires custom behaviour.
